transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess I came in because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It’s hard to explain. Like… I used to be Ruben, you know, I could talk to anybody, customers, strangers in line, didn’t matter. I was good at that. My wife used to joke I could sell air conditioning to somebody in Alaska.

But lately it’s like that guy’s just… gone. I wake up and there’s this weight there before I even get out of bed. So, yeah, that’s why I’m here.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. It’s been about eight months now. Around when the new regional manager started, and he just… started riding me hard, taking accounts from me that I’d handled for years.

Those weren’t just names on a list, you know? I knew those people, their kids sometimes, what kind of coffee they drank when I stopped by. And then suddenly I’m being treated like I don’t know how to do my own job. So… yeah, that’s when it really started.
Before this started eight months ago, had you already been feeling down most days for two years or more?

No… not two years. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, sure, everybody does—sales has its ups and downs, and some months you’re chasing people who suddenly won’t return your calls. But this… this really started about eight months ago, when that new regional manager came in and started coming down on me, taking accounts I’d worked for years. That’s when it turned into most days feeling like this.
If the situation with your new regional manager were resolved, do you think you’d still feel this way?

I don’t know… I’d like to think if he backed off, maybe some of the pressure would lift. But this feeling I wake up with most days, that heavy, hollow thing in my chest… it feels like it’s already settled into me.

Like, I keep thinking if work got fixed, maybe I’d snap back to being the old Ruben, the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy the day. But right now that guy feels pretty far away.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I used to really look forward to things. Bowling night, messing around in the garden, taking my wife to those little gallery shows she likes… we used to go dancing too, not that I was ever any good, but she’d laugh and it was fun.

Now I just… I sit there and come up with reasons not to go. Like the yard can wait, or I’m too tired for the gallery, or bowling’s not worth driving over there. It’s not even that I hate those things now. It’s more like none of it feels worth the effort anymore.
How has your sleep been lately?

Not good. I mean, I get into bed and I’m exhausted, but then my brain starts running—mostly work stuff, conversations I should’ve handled differently, what he’s going to say next, accounts, numbers… I just lie there staring at the ceiling.

And then if I do finally fall asleep, I’m up at like three or four in the morning. My dad used to wake up early like that for fishing, but that was different, he’d be excited to go. I wake up already feeling worn out, just… dreading having to start the day.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yeah… I’ve had thoughts like that. Not like—I don’t know how to say it right. I’ll be lying there and think maybe my wife and the kids would be better off if I just didn’t wake up.

And then I think about my wife making coffee in the morning, she always leaves the spoon in the sink even though I tease her about it, and… I don’t know, it scares me. Those thoughts scare me. I don’t trust myself the way I used to.
Have you thought about how you might kill yourself?

I… I don’t know. I haven’t really made some kind of plan, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like these thoughts come in at night, like maybe my wife and kids would be better off if I just didn’t wake up.

And then I’ll think about them sitting at the kitchen table, or my wife doing her usual little routine in the morning, and I get scared. I don’t like that those thoughts are even in my head. I don’t trust myself the way I used to.
Before these past eight months, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, like anybody, I guess. Sales is up and down, and there were times after a bad quarter where I’d come home and just sit in the driveway for a while before going in. My dad used to say you leave work at work, but he never had emails following him around in his pocket, you know?

But depressed like this, for two weeks or more… I don’t know. I can’t really say. Nothing comes to mind the same way this has been.
Before these past eight months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don’t know… I keep trying to think back, but it’s all kind of blurry. I mean, there were times I was down, sure. Everybody gets worn out, right? Especially in sales—one bad month turns into three, and then you’re staring at your numbers like they’re going to magically change.

But nearly every day for two weeks, losing interest in things… I can’t say for sure. Nothing stands out to me the way this does. Maybe I had rough patches, but I don’t remember it being like this.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yeah… yeah, I have. I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like all those years of taking care of clients, keeping relationships going, being the guy people could count on… it doesn’t mean anything anymore because I can’t even seem to handle the job now.

And then I start thinking about my family, you know, how I was supposed to be providing and keeping things steady. My wife always used to say I knew how to talk to anybody, that I could sell ice in winter, stupid stuff like that… and now I just feel like I’m not that person. Like I’ve failed at the one thing I was supposed to be good for.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things on most days?

I don’t know if I’d call it “worrying excessively.” I mean, I think about things a lot, sure… work, money, whether I’m doing what I’m supposed to be doing. But then again, that’s kind of been my life in sales—always thinking about the next account, the next call, who’s going to renew and who’s going to disappear on you.

My wife used to tell me I’d be halfway through dinner and still mentally writing an email to some client, and I’d say, “No, no, I’m listening,” but I probably wasn’t. So… I guess I worry, but most days, excessively? I’m not sure. It all kind of blends together lately.
Compared with what your manager has been doing at work, does your reaction feel stronger than you would normally expect for that kind of stress?

I’m not sure how to measure that, honestly. I mean, managers push—that’s what they do, right? I’ve had managers before who rode people hard, and you just learn to nod and go make the calls.

This one… I don’t know. Sometimes I think maybe I’m taking it too personally, but then I start thinking about all the little comments, the meetings, the numbers, and it just gets all tangled up. I used to know how to handle pressure better, or at least I think I did. Back when I first started, we had this regional guy who would come in with these ridiculous pep talks—charts everywhere, pointing at everyone like we were in boot camp—and we’d all laugh about it after.

Now I don’t really laugh about it. But whether that means my reaction is stronger than it should be… I don’t know. I can’t really tell anymore.
Before these past eight months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, sure. Everybody does, right? There were times when work was rough or money was tight, or after my kids were giving us headaches when they were younger—well, teenagers, that’s a whole different thing.

But depressed nearly every day for two weeks… I don’t know if I ever kept track of it like that. I usually just pushed through, went to work, made the calls, came home. Back then I didn’t really think in those terms. So I can’t honestly say.
Before these past eight months, was there ever a time in your life when you lost interest in almost everything for at least two weeks?

Before these past eight months? I don’t know… I mean, I always had things I liked doing. Bowling on Thursdays, messing around in the garden when the weather was decent. My wife likes these little gallery shows downtown, and I used to take her, make a night of it, maybe go dancing after if my knees weren’t complaining too much.

Lately it’s different. Now I just kind of sit there and come up with reasons not to go. “I’m tired,” or “maybe next weekend,” that kind of thing. It’s not that I hate those things… it’s just none of it feels worth the effort anymore.

But before this stretch? I can’t really remember losing interest like that for two weeks or whatever. Not the way it is now.
Before these past eight months, was there ever another time when you felt down nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Before this? I’m not sure there was another time like this. I mean, I’ve had lousy weeks, everybody has, especially in sales—you lose an account, someone doesn’t call back, you start wondering if you still know how to talk to people.

But what brought me in now is… most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Like the old Ruben, the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy the day, is just gone somewhere. I don’t really remember feeling that way nearly every day before these past months.
Before these past eight months, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks and it clearly stood out from your usual self?

I don’t think so, not before this. I mean, I’ve had bad moods, sure—sales will do that to you, you know, one day you’re everyone’s best friend and the next nobody returns your calls.

But this time is what stands out. That’s why I came in. Most days I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling right here in my chest, like the old Ruben—the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day—is just… gone. I don’t remember anything before that feeling like this.
Do you still feel this depressed on days when you’re away from work, like weekends or vacation days?

Yeah… yeah, it’s still there. Weekends don’t really change it much.

I used to think, you know, maybe it was just work wearing me down—sales calls, driving all over, trying to sound upbeat for people who barely want to listen. But even if I’m not working, I wake up with that same heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Like the old me, the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy the day, is just… not around.
Aside from work, have you been blaming yourself a lot about other parts of your life?

Yeah… I do. It’s not just work exactly, though that’s where my mind goes first.

I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like all those years of taking care of clients, being the guy people could count on, providing for my family… somehow none of it counts anymore because I can’t even handle this job the way I used to.

And then I’ll start thinking about stupid things, like old customers who used to call me directly, or how I used to know every diner off the highway where you could get decent coffee before a meeting… I don’t know why that pops in my head. But it all comes back to the same thing: I feel like I’m not worth much lately.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I mean, my mind wanders, sure, but it’s hard to tell if that’s concentration or just… getting older, or being tired of the same conversations over and over.

Like with sales, you learn to listen for certain words—budget, timeline, decision-maker—and sometimes people will talk for twenty minutes about their cousin’s roofing business before they ever get to the point. I used to be pretty good at following all that.

Lately… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m concentrating worse or not. What do you mean exactly—like reading something and not taking it in, or forgetting what someone just said?

Before this? I’m not sure there was another time like this. I mean, I’ve had lousy weeks, everybody has, especially in sales—you lose an account, someone doesn’t call back, you start wondering if you still know how to talk to people.

But what brought me in now is… most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Like the old Ruben, the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy the day, is just gone somewhere. I don’t really remember feeling that way nearly every day before these past months.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I do. It’s not just work exactly, though that’s where my mind goes first.

I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like all those years of taking care of clients, being the guy people could count on, providing for my family… somehow none of it counts anymore because I can’t even handle this job the way I used to.

And then I’ll start thinking about stupid things, like old customers who used to call me directly, or how I used to know every diner off the highway where you could get decent coffee before a meeting… I don’t know why that pops in my head. But it all comes back to the same thing: I feel like I’m not worth much lately.

I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I mean, my mind wanders, sure, but it’s hard to tell if that’s concentration or just… getting older, or being tired of the same conversations over and over.

Like with sales, you learn to listen for certain words—budget, timeline, decision-maker—and sometimes people will talk for twenty minutes about their cousin’s roofing business before they ever get to the point. I used to be pretty good at following all that.

Lately… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m concentrating worse or not. What do you mean exactly—like reading something and not taking it in, or forgetting what someone just said?
